profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA. It trades on the exchange under the ticker NVDA and reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing. The company holds CIK 0001045810 with the SEC.

On the AI side, NVIDIA's site describes the Nemotron family as a set of multimodal, open AI models built for agentic workflows, covering reasoning, vision, speech, retrieval-augmented generation, and safety tasks. The site states that Nemotron models are available under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA, and that NVIDIA publishes training datasets, techniques, and model weights alongside the releases. The site also names specific components including Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for specialized task completion and NeMo Switchyard for routing tasks across models, with platform support cited for NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark. Bryan Catanzaro, described as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is mentioned in connection with the project's direction. ServiceNow is named as a partner that evaluated Nemotron for visual question-and-answer accuracy.

NVIDIA also offers NIM, described on the site as inference microservices for deploying foundation models with enterprise GPU optimization and self-hosted options, available at build.nvidia.com and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production use. Additional tools mentioned on the site include NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, NeMo, and NVIDIA Blueprints, alongside support for open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. No litigation or MCP server registrations are recorded in the held facts for this company.
